Learn My Way

Learning platform

  • UX
  • UI
  • CSS
  • Angular
  • Adapt

The Learn My Way platform teaches users with little or no digital experience how to use the internet. It's a service provided by Good Things Foundation. It replaces an old system which was becoming unmanageable & needed a UX update to modernise it.

The challenge

Due to its users being digitally inexperienced (and often complete novices) we had to work out a way to guide them through the site as simply as possible and provide useful learning resources written in plain language which addressed their concerns and made them feel they were practicing in a safe environment.

Learn My Way's user base is wide and varied encompassing non-native English speakers, people with learning disabilities and a lot of older people needing to get comfortable being online.

What I did

I had a few roles on this project:

  1. I helped gather UX requirements (including opinions and feedback on the old system and user research) and I created several levels of prototype (from low-fidelity wireframes to high fidelity and clickable) to validate our assumptions. We tested each step on a cohort of Good Things' network of organisations who support digitally excluded people. From there I worked up the user journeys.
  2. From the extensive feedback, I created a lot of UI work in Sketch, including a style guide for junior developers to follow. We showed the organisations again to test colour combinations, positioning of elements and overall feel. We needed to provide a level of continuity from the very well-used old product so the interface felt just familiar enough to promote a smooth transition for existing users and staff/volunteers.
  3. I wrote all the micro-copy for the UI - we needed to not use jargon (things like 'button' and 'link') and provide extremely clear and simple instructions due to the user base.
  4. During the development phase, I learned a bit of Angular and used HTML5 and CSS3 to implement the interface. I also advised more junior team members on their work to keep the design and feel tight.
  5. I made sure the product had a good level of accessibility using WCAG guidelines. One limitation was the Adapt Learning content which was difficult (and time consuming) to modify to bring it up to modern standards.

What we achieved

During the project, Good Things went through an organisational restructure so we had to scale back our ambitions with the loss of team members and a truncation of the timeline. We had to be flexible and responsive to a changing environment so we came up with a simple, highly usable iteration which satisfied the needs of the users and was launched on time.
